layoutReference: First desktop HTML layout, 960 by approximately 1216 CSS pixels, before artwork
role: Illustrative orbital background only. It does not show observed satellite positions or generate the data, marks or text.
prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: background plate for a factual orbital-traffic poster, portrait 4:5 composition.
Input image 1 is a layout reference only. It shows where real HTML typography, numerical labels, controls, and two circular dot charts will later be overlaid. Generate ONLY the background image. Remove ALL of the reference's words, numbers, dots, divider, buttons and data graphics, leaving empty dark space in their occupied regions. Do not reproduce the infographic.
Scene: a restrained, realistic view from low Earth orbit, deep blue-black vacuum and an extremely subdued curved Earth limb, atmospheric blue haze, dark ocean and faint soft cloud texture near the lower right edge. It should feel like real space photography, not a game HUD.
Composition informed by the layout: the top-left headline area and both circular chart areas must remain smooth, very dark and almost featureless. There is a small open area in the upper right (about x=78-96%, y=9-20% of the canvas) where a single small, physically plausible uncrewed satellite can sit, angled naturally: a compact gold-foil instrument bus, two connected rectangular solar-panel wings with believable attachment and a modest antenna. Keep its entire silhouette within that empty area, away from the headline and the top source strip. No logos or recognizable brand. Let the Earth curve enter quietly at the lower-right edge, below the dot fields, with its brightest thin blue rim limited to the right margin and the open band above the footnote. Keep the footnote region very dark.
Palette: midnight navy centered on #0a1c2a, faint cool atmospheric blue, restrained metallic reflection on the satellite. The whole plate is intentionally low contrast, with the spacecraft clearly subordinate to large bright text and chart marks added later.
Lighting: believable distant sunlight from the upper right, subtle reflections, no lens flare, no dramatic bright bloom.
Constraints: no text, numbers, symbols, grids, interface elements, diagrams, charts, colored data dots, dense star fields, bright city-light specks, explosions, asteroid belts or additional spacecraft. Objects and details must occupy the actual open regions shown by the reference. The result is illustrative artwork, not evidence of satellite positions.
